40 undertakers here submitted a
petition to the House District Com
mittee late yesterday, asking that
open hearings be held on bill
which has passed the Senate, re-
quiring that undertakers be licensed.

ator Bilbo, Democrat, of Mississippi
and passed the Senate July 7, with
out any hearings being held. It
would set up an examining board of
seven, six of whom would be under
takers, to pass on the qualifications,
training and experience of all those
seeking an undertakers or en-
balmer's license.


The petition declares that "if
Congress gives power to these six
undertakers to control the entire
undertaking business in the Dis
trict of Columbia, we feel it would
create a monopoly by few persons
that would definitely work a hard
ship in the performance of our du-
ties."


"The bill is being run through
Congress," the petitioners say, with
out their having been given an op-
portunity to express their opposi-
tion. President Roosevelt vetoed
similar legislation two years ago,
they point out. The President
argued then that the District Com
missioners already have sufficient
authority to regulate and control
the practices of members of their
profession.
